owner.orgHelp: The organisation you want to deploy from. You need permission to create GitHub Apps there.
owner.orgInvalid: Use the organisation's login: letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 39 characters.
owner.allowOthers: Allow other accounts and organisations to install it
owner.publicHelp: Any GitHub account or organisation can install this App. Pick this when you deploy from several organisations.
owner.privatePersonalHelp: Private: the App can only be installed on your personal account. Choose an organisation above, or allow other accounts, to deploy from an organisation.
owner.privateOrgHelp: Private: the App can only be installed on this organisation. Allow other accounts to also install it on your personal account or other organisations.

githubApp.notInstalled: The App was created but has not been installed on an account or organisation yet. Finish installing it on GitHub to pick repositories. A private App can only be installed on the account or organisation that owns it.

githubAppOrg.addOrgHelp: GitHub shows the accounts you can install on. Pick the organisation. If you are not an owner, GitHub sends the request to its owners.
githubAppOrg.privateBody: To add an organisation, open the App's Advanced settings, choose Make public (Any account), then come back and press Add organisation. Or register a new App owned by the organisation.
githubAppOrg.noSlug: This connection was registered before Levelrail could remember the App's install link. Reconnect the App above (or use manual setup) to enable Add organisation here.

backups.description: Where backups and artefacts are kept.

organizations.title: Organisations
organizations.description: Group related projects under an organisation.

bitbucket-server-app.description: Bitbucket Server and Data Centre repository access with a personal access token.

bitbucket_server.description: Connect Bitbucket Server or Data Centre with a personal access token for repository browsing and webhook-driven deploys.

azure_devops.description: Connect an Azure DevOps organisation with a personal access token for repository browsing and push-driven deploys. Repositories show as PROJECT/repo.

width.comfortableHint: Centred column with generous side margins

organizationsPage.title: Organisations
organizationsPage.description: Group related projects under an organisation. File a project into one from the project's own detail page.

profile.readOnly: Only organisation admins can edit the profile.
profile.slugDefault: The default organisation cannot have a slug.

avatar.removeBody: The organisation goes back to its initials.

scopes.ghcr: read:packages to pull, write:packages to push. For an SSO-enforced organisation, authorise the token for SSO.

description.gitlab: Register a GitLab OAuth application, then authorise it. gitlab.com and self-managed instances can be connected side by side.
description.bitbucket: Register a Bitbucket OAuth consumer, then authorise it. Add a second consumer later for another workspace.
description.gitea: Register a Gitea OAuth application, then authorise it. Each Gitea or Forgejo server is its own connection.
description.forgejo: Register a Forgejo OAuth application, then authorise it. Codeberg and self-hosted servers are each their own connection.
description.azure_devops: Create a personal access token in your Azure DevOps organisation, then add it here.

add.description: Create the OAuth application on the provider with redirect URI {{callback}}, then enter it here. You will be sent to the provider to authorise it.
add.labelHelp: Defaults to the account name once you authorise. You can rename it later.
add.instanceHelpAzure: Your organisation address, for example https://dev.azure.com/ORG.

toast.addedBody: Authorise it with the provider to finish.

banner.whatFor: Connect one account per person, team or organisation. Apps stay tied to the account they were created from, so you can add or remove accounts without touching your apps.

github.asks: You will create or pick a GitHub App and install it on an account or organisation.

azure_devops.asks: You will paste your organisation URL and a personal access token.

emailBranding.description: The logo, accent colour and footer every rich email shares: password resets, invites, alerts and announcements.
emailBranding.colorHint: A six digit hex value such as #107292. Leave empty to use the brand colour.
emailBranding.invalidColor: Use a six digit hex colour such as #107292.

darkBase.description: The surface colour used in dark mode.

lightBase.description: The surface colour used in light mode.
